## Functions

A function's effect puts it in one of three parts. A total function answers every input in the ranges it declares. ### Total

#### `split`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes `total`, and kaname holds it to that.

Each line gets the refund up to its end less the refund before it.

```kn
fn split(lines: list[Line] count >=1 <=10, refund: money[USDc] range >=0USDc <=10_000_000USDc) -> list[money[USDc]] total
  description "Each line gets the refund up to its end less the refund before it"
  map(running_totals(lines, l => l.left), r => allocate(refund, r.upto, r.total) - allocate(refund, r.before, r.total))
```

## Properties

A property claims that for every input in the ranges its parameters declare, and on which its `when` lines hold, its last line is `true`. `kaname check` tries it on the vectors and reports a counterexample as E603; it is shown only when `--lean` takes a proof of it. This page shows what each property says, not its answer.

### `every_line_gets_a_share`

A refund of more than nothing gives every line something.

```kn
property every_line_gets_a_share(lines: list[Line] count >=1 <=10, refund: money[USDc] range >=0USDc <=10_000_000USDc)
  description "A refund of more than nothing gives every line something"
  when refund > 0USDc
  let shares = split(lines: lines, refund: refund)
  all(shares, s => s > 0USDc)
```

It writes 1 `when` line. Its last line is `all(shares, s => s > 0USDc)`.

No proof file `shares.lean` is beside the .kn.
